attributes.Descriptions: All floaters must exit the river here. Floating beyond this point is extremely dangerous and should not be attempted. An ADA compliant concrete ramp is located just downstream on river-left.
attributes.Name: Last Chance Take-Out Ann Morrison Park

attributes.Descriptions: Bubb Dam Rapid is a diversion dam with a 2-3 foot drop. Stay in the middle of the river, as this dam diverts water into Gallagher Canal. Class II rapids are rapids where maneuvering is required prior to entering the rapid. Waves may be large. Always exercise caution when approaching and navigating any rapid.
attributes.Name: Bubb Dam Rapid (Rapid 1 - Class II)

attributes.Descriptions: Beach stairs and boat ramp areas designated for launching from Barber Park. The beach area includes an ADA compliant concrete ramp.
attributes.Name: Barber Park Put-In

attributes.Descriptions: Rock Garden Rapid is a diversion dam with a swift green tongue down the right side. Many rocks form this diversion dam at a steep angle from upstream right to downstream left. Rocks on the downstream left side are a known hazard and can cause floaters to get hung up or puncture vessels. Take the right-side approach just after passing beneath the overhead power lines in the fastest moving water. This dam diverts water into Loggers Creek. Class II rapids are rapids where paddling is required prior to entering the rapid. Waves may be large. Always exercise care when approaching and navigating any rapid.
attributes.Name: Rock Garden Rapid (Rapid 2 - Class II)

attributes.Descriptions: Mesa Rapid is a diversion dam with a slow-moving pool that requires active paddling  upon approach. The diversion is angled upstream-left to downstream-right, diverting water into the Boise City Canal. The run is wide with a pour-over 1-2 foot drop. There is a swift green tongue down the right of center side, but floaters should paddle away from the tree branches on the right of the river, below the wave. Class II rapids are rapids where paddling is required prior to entering the rapid. Waves may be large. Always exercise care when approaching and navigating any rapid.
attributes.Name: Mesa Rapid (Rapid 3 - Class II)

attributes.Descriptions: OVEARHEAD HAZARD: People, debris, or other objects may suddenly enter or fall into the river at any time. Be alert to the actions of others and how they may affect your safety. According to city code, it is illegal for any person to jump from or to throw or drop any object, including a person, from any bridge, tree, or other landscape features into the Boise River within fifty feet (50') of any boater, floater, rafter or tuber.
attributes.Name: Baybrook Bridge

attributes.Descriptions: The float near Kristin Armstrong Municipal Park is generally a swift ride with the current running down the right bank. Stay in the middle of the river to avoid branches and low hanging trees on river-right. The photo provided is a representation of a low hanging tree and not necessarily the specific tree encountered at this location.

attributes.Descriptions: Deep, strong currents exist here that require hard paddling to maneuver through the bridge piers that extend into the water. Paddle down the middle of the river to stay right of the first pier and left of the second pier. Tying rafts or tubes together is extremely dangerous especially when approaching bridges. People, debris, or other objects may suddenly enter or fall into the river at any time. Be alert to the actions of others and how they may affect your safety.
